statement: A business that owns or licenses computerized data including personal information must disclose a breach of the security of the system to each California resident whose unencrypted personal information was, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired by an unauthorized person (Civil Code § 1798.82(a)(1)); the disclosure is due within 30 calendar days of discovery or notification of the breach (§ 1798.82(a)(2)(A)), with delay permitted for the legitimate needs of law enforcement or as necessary to determine the scope of the breach and restore the reasonable integrity of the data system (§§ 1798.82(a)(2)(B), (c)).
caveat: The 30-calendar-day deadline is the section text current as of January 1, 2026; the prior standard was notification in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, and that older wording still circulates in guidance (and remains in Civil Code § 1798.29 for state agencies). The duty also reaches encrypted data when the encryption key or security credential is reasonably believed compromised. Whether an incident is a reportable breach, and which other states' statutes apply, are fact questions this repo does not decide.
